audit.why: 53.44% over 2631 games. EVEN 5.5/10 stands: Ahri owns levels 1-6, Anivia owns the item phases.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart was 'Skill' on every row while content and packet read Ahri x5 then Anivia, Anivia. The content 'whys' were also shifted a row: whys[4] said level 6 flips to Anivia while win[4] said Ahri.
audit.why: phases[N].side and win[N] are the same row, and whys[N] must agree with win[N].
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side -> Ahri, phases[5..6].side -> Anivia; whys[4] and whys[5] realigned; content 'mid' no longer says level 6 flips.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction — Frostbite doubling its damage on a target recently hit by Flash Frost or standing in a fully formed Glacial Storm — was only hinted at. spikes[3] claimed Glacial Storm 'reduces armor/MR', which it does not; it damages and slows.
audit.why: Riot text for E: damage is doubled if the target was recently hit by Flash Frost or damaged by a fully formed Glacial Storm. R text is damage plus slow only.
audit.corrected: Stated in report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[2].d, enemyWin, spikes[3].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: No numbers. Also the wrong spell was framed as the punishable cooldown.
audit.why: Frostbite is a 4s cooldown, so it is never 'down'; Flash Frost at 11s rank 1 and Crystallize at 17s are the two real windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flash Frost's 1075 range beating both your Q (970) and Charm (975) was never stated.
audit.why: She wins the range war; your answer is dodging the slow sphere, not out-ranging it.

edits.before: Q both ways through the wave on his last-hits — the true-damage return is most of your early poke.

edits.before: Anivia wins by landing Flash Frost (Stun), denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Anivia wins by stunning you with Flash Frost, doubling Frostbite on the chilled target, and holding you inside Glacial Storm.

edits.before: - Anivia Flash Frost (Stun): matchup-defining — The slow-moving stun starts every Anivia kill — sidestep it and her E never doubles. Check it before every step-up. - R Spirit Rush (last dash) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Flash Frost is 11s at rank 1 and travels slowly at 1075 range — dodge the sphere and Frostbite's double damage never happens. - Frostbite is only 4s, so the stun, not the nuke, is the cooldown you count. - Crystallize is 17s: hold a Spirit Rush dash for after the wall drops.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry by punishing whiffs: Flash Frost is 11s, and every miss is a free Charm combo before Glacial Storm forms.

edits.before: Track Anivia’s Flash Frost (Stun): The slow-moving stun starts every Anivia kill — sidestep it and her E never doubles. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Frostbite doubles only on a target recently hit by Flash Frost or sitting in a fully formed Glacial Storm — dodge the sphere, then leave the storm.

edits.before: Q through his last-hit so both hits land, W if he eats the return, and walk — repeat until the charm window is lethal instead of optimistic.
edits.after: Rebirth means her first death is fake — hold Charm for the egg so she cannot walk away while it hatches, and keep Ignite for that same moment.

edits.before: Anivia spends Flash Frost (Stun) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Her Flash Frost costs 80 mana at rank 1 — heal off full clears and she runs out of poke first.

edits.before: That’s Anivia’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Crystallize is a wall that eats a dash — spend all three and it traps you.

edits.before: Charming on cooldown for chip damage and then facing his real engage with nothing — the charm is the matchup, not the poke.
edits.after: Trading while Flash Frost is loaded hands her the stun, and Frostbite doubles on anything the sphere already chilled.

edits.before: Level 6 flips to Anivia — Rebirth baits out your all-in cooldowns for a bad trade
edits.after: Level 6 stays yours — Spirit Rush dashes dodge Flash Frost and set your charm angles

edits.before: 2+ items favors Anivia as Crystallize walls neutralize your dash-based escapes
edits.after: First item favors Anivia as a 17s Crystallize wall cuts your dash escape lines

edits.before: Level 6 flips against you: Rebirth turns any all-in into a two-phase fight, and if you don't respect the egg form her follow-up Glacial Storm can turn the tables, so you need to bait Flash Frost or wait for her to misposition before committing your ultimate.
edits.after: Level 6 still leans your way: Spirit Rush's three dashes dodge Flash Frost outright, but Rebirth turns any all-in into a two-phase fight, so bait the sphere and keep a dash to leave once the egg soaks the burst you meant for her.

edits.before: Late-game Anivia's Glacial Storm zones half the fight and reduces armor/MR structures around it, so she out-scales your poke-and-roam profile in a straight teamfight if left unchecked.
edits.after: Late-game Glacial Storm slows everything inside it and makes Frostbite double on anyone caught there, so she out-zones your poke-and-roam profile unless you flank around the storm entirely.
